batch: prune19; baseline is turn-start worktree, not HEAD
changes: A10: expand the existing keyed snapshot mechanism from three to 45 tables. Changed normal-table rows are deleted together then inserted, allowing secondary UNIQUE values to be exchanged while retaining untouched rows. Original three hot tables retain UPSERT. No second persistence framework or caller dirty flags.

Two non-text-keyed projections (voice_profiles and founder_vision), and legacy invalid-key rows, retain atomic table replacement. Snapshots still finish synchronously before SQL awaits, with fingerprints published only after COMMIT.
Use stable persistenceTimestamp fallback for legacy memory avatars instead of generating new dates on each save.

A10: generated archive registration returns its durable entry; files/save reuses it instead of repeated archive lookups and duplicate metadata setup. Recheck source ownership immediately after awaiting archive registration. files/list passes the already-read directory set to avoid per-entry existsSync calls.
A11: AvatarStudio palette derives from the current pet, deleting duplicate state/effect and duplicate initial localStorage read.

A12: two chat tests share the production-callback fixture. No test cases removed; preserves attachment defaults and pending-conversation state setter behavior. One new test-only helper, no new business module.

addedTests.name: D:/lumiOS/test/database_snapshot_batch.test.ts::snapshot batch persistence exchanges unique usernames without rewriting untouched users, and retains all rows on failure

regressionCoverage: Actual SQLite username exchange updates only the two changed users; a conflicting exchange rolls back and can be retried, then survives reopen
Existing no-op flush test also covers missing-date avatars
Single-file archive lookup and directory-set listing return identical IDs, with no per-file existence probes for the latter
Prior 6537 cases preserved by file/full-name multiset, one new case

performance.method: Real writeDB/flushDBOrThrow against isolated SQLite. N conversation rows plus N setting rows in each size. Two warmups and six measured samples per mode, with process GC before timing; total_changes queries outside timing. Before/after order alternates at 10000. No concurrent build/full-suite jobs. Exactly two reusable synthetic data roots.
performance.sourceTiming: Bundles were built before the later missing-avatar-timestamp fallback edit. The benchmark has no avatar fixtures; that fix is covered by the final test suite, not this performance measurement.
performance.physicalWrites: changedRows is SQLite total_changes delta. An updated ordinary keyed row uses one DELETE plus one INSERT, hence 2 physical changes; it is not two logical records.
performance.regression: No-change 30000+30000-row flush median increased from 43.10 to 63.72 ms. Row-key tracking has overhead; this is not an across-the-board speed improvement.
performance.scope: Synthetic persistence benchmark only, not live model/API/chat/desktop latency; no peak-memory claim.

remaining: All rows still scanned and serialized to catch raw aliases and nested in-place changes. Removing this safely requires converging mutation entry points, not simply trusting object identity.
voice_profiles, founder_vision and legacy invalid keys retain replacement snapshots. Bulk changed rows still captured before SQL awaits.
Archive JSON readIndex remains synchronous; directory-set reuse removes redundant existence checks, not JSON parsing or all IO.
Other complex UI state, old structural tests, execution projections and real-client acceptance remain within the whole-project audit. This batch does not close them.
limits: No live model/API calls or client launch/restart
No subagents; existing dirty worktree preserved
